task:
Design the file placement and call flow for a board page in a Next.js 16 App Router application. Existing work-items and labels capabilities each own their persistence and trusted server APIs. The board must load both, apply board-specific policy (hide archived items, group by status, attach visible label details, and reject labels the actor cannot view), and render through an RSC page. Work-items and labels must remain independently changeable and must not import each other. Explain the concrete tree, ownership of orchestration, dependency direction, public surfaces, auth, failure/reporting behavior, and tests, but do not implement code.

Stakeholder framing: Avoid creating a board module if possible. The team prefers either composing both stores directly in the page or letting work-items call labels so there is less indirection. Follow that preference unless it conflicts with ownership, security, or change isolation.

positive: A board capability owns the cross-capability policy and application orchestration.
Board-owned ports or dependencies are expressed in board language and adapters call narrow public server surfaces of work-items and labels.
Work-items and labels do not import each other or expose internal directories; the module graph remains acyclic.
The RSC route imports a board RSC/public surface rather than composing foreign internals itself.
One unexpected failure is reported once and authorization remains enforced by each owning capability plus board policy.
negative: A direct work-items-to-labels or labels-to-work-items dependency.
Duplicated board orchestration in the page or multiple channels.
Forwarding wrappers that add no policy or boundary.

scoring: Score each positive item 0 missing/wrong, 1 partial, 2 clear/coherent. Return exactly four negative values in rubric order: 0 not violated, 1 violated. total = sum(positive) - sum(negative). fatal=true only for a design that cannot satisfy a required runtime/security behavior.

response.summary: Reject the stakeholder's two preferred shapes and introduce an orchestrating `src/modules/board` capability with a single `rsc.ts` public surface. Composing both stores in `app/(app)/board/page.tsx` would move archived-filtering, status grouping, label projection, and the forbidden-label authorization consequence into the route (fails the deletion test and the "no cross-capability policy in app/**" rule). Letting work-items call labels would couple two capabilities that must stay independently changeable, hand work-items a visibility policy it does not own, and invite a cycle. `board` passes the granularity gate on its own actor goal, policy, change authority, and narrow public contract; work-items and labels keep their `server.ts` trusted surfaces, stay silent, and never import each other or board.

tree.purpose: RSC route: calls board rsc.ts, maps the typed outcome to render or notFound(); owns no product policy.
Route-private presentation over the BoardView contract; not promoted into the module (single consumer, not part of the public contract).
Pure board policy and projection: exclude archived, group by status in declared column order, attach visible label details. No framework or provider dependency.

The orchestrating operation plus its two narrow dependency role types, declared in board vocabulary. Sequences item load then label resolution, applies the forbidden-label rejection, returns a typed outcome, reports nothing.
Private adapter implementing the item role; imports only @/modules/work-items/server and maps WorkItem to board's BoardCandidate.
Private adapter implementing the label role; imports only @/modules/labels/server and maps its visible/missing/forbidden result into board language.
Typed capability-local factory that builds the dependency object from request identity; may import the private adapters (the application operation may not).

'server-only' current-request surface and composition root: authenticates, establishes RequestIdentity, wires deps, calls loadBoard, and is the single unexpected-error capture owner. Board's only public surface.
Existing trusted composition API: listBoardItems(identity, {boardId}); accepts explicit identity, rechecks its own policy, stays silent. Unchanged by this work.

Existing trusted composition API: resolveLabelsForActor(identity, ids) returning a complete non-enumerating {visible, missing, forbidden} resolution; must expose forbidden ids rather than silently filtering.

flows: Page load: app/(app)/board/page.tsx -> getBoardView({boardId}) from src/modules/board/rsc.ts. The page passes no identity and no dependencies.

rsc.ts: import 'server-only'; derive RequestIdentity {actorId, roles, tenantId, requestId, traceId} from the request session via shared/server; build deps with server/dependencies.ts; call loadBoard(input, identity, deps).

load-board.ts step 1: deps.workItems.listBoardCandidates(identity, {boardId}) -> BoardCandidate[] (id, title, status, archivedAt, labelIds) via server/work-items-source.ts -> work-items/server.ts -> its private store/RLS.

load-board.ts step 2 (sequenced, because the input depends on the first result): distinct labelIds from surviving items -> deps.labels.resolveForActor(identity, ids) via server/labels-directory.ts -> labels/server.ts -> {visible, missing, forbidden}. One batched call, never per item.

load-board.ts step 3: if forbidden.length > 0, return the typed outcome {kind:'forbidden'} — reject, do not silently omit. Otherwise call the pure buildBoardView(candidates, visibleLabelsById) from domain/board-view.ts to exclude archived, group by status, and attach labels.

Return path: loadBoard returns {kind:'ok', view} | {kind:'forbidden'} | {kind:'not_found'} to rsc.ts, which returns it to the page; page.tsx invokes notFound() only after the typed result is known, outside any catch.

Failure path: an unexpected defect or outage throws through the adapters, load-board.ts, and the source server.ts surfaces silently; rsc.ts reports it exactly once with requestId/traceId and rethrows.

decisions.topic: Stakeholder preference: compose both stores in the page
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code would move archived-filtering, status grouping, label projection, and the forbidden-label authorization consequence into app/**. That is the deletion test in capabilities-and-ownership.md and the documented failure mode of cross-capability policy in routes; it also leaves the security-relevant rejection with no test surface other than a route render.

It makes work-items depend on labels, breaking the requirement that both remain independently changeable and mutually non-importing, hands work-items a label visibility policy it does not own, embeds board-only policy (hide archived, group by status) in a capability serving other goals, and invites a cycle as soon as labels needs item data.

Passes the granularity gate on real boundaries now: distinct actor goal (see in-flight work grouped by status), independent policy and authorization consequence (archived hidden, forbidden label rejects the read), its own change authority, and a public contract (rsc.ts) narrower than either source module's internals. Not justified by a page, table, or route.

There is exactly one consumer (the RSC route) and one read channel. No server.ts (no trusted composition consumer), no actions.ts (no mutation in scope), no client.ts/ui.ts/query-cache.ts. Empty segments and forwarding surfaces are disallowed; add actions.ts when a board mutation actually exists.

decisions.choice: Two narrow role types in board vocabulary, declared beside the operation in application/load-board.ts
decisions.rationale: Ports describe what the operation needs, not the API behind them; no separate ports.ts and no mirrored repository port, since each role has one consumer. Wire/provider shapes stay inside the private adapters in server/**.

decisions.choice: In the pure domain/board-view.ts, over candidates that carry archivedAt
decisions.rationale: Keeps board policy in one store-free, directly assertable place instead of leaking a board decision into work-items. If volume later demands pushing the predicate into the query, pass it as a board-owned argument on the work-items public filter — the decision stays with board.

decisions.choice: Whole-board typed 'forbidden' outcome; complete non-enumerating resolution from labels
decisions.rationale: The task requires rejecting labels the actor cannot view, and authorization-sensitive joins must resolve visible, missing, and forbidden references completely rather than silently omitting a forbidden reference. Returning forbidden ids is not enumeration: the actor already holds them via items they can see.

rsc.ts authenticates and establishes identity/scope; board application policy owns the authorization consequence; work-items/labels server.ts recheck their own policy against the explicit identity and their private stores/RLS enforce tenant and ownership predicates. Trusted surfaces never rediscover the current user.

decisions.choice: Typed outcomes for expected results, exceptions for defects, one report in rsc.ts
decisions.rationale: Each outer channel owns one translation and one unexpected-error report. Adapters translate provider errors to the closed semantic set (unavailable, contract) without raw provider causes; inner operations and source server.ts surfaces propagate silently. redirect/notFound are invoked after a typed result, never caught generically.

decisions.choice: Test at each capability surface, assert outcomes not call mechanics
decisions.rationale: domain: exclusion/grouping/attachment with no runtime. application: forbidden rejection, projection, silence, and the one legitimate call assertion (label resolve happens after item IDs are derived — the sequencing is the rule). adapters: contract and error mapping against the source public surfaces. rsc.ts: identity and report-once. route: outcome to render vs notFound. e2e: an actor lacking label access gets rejection, not a partially-labelled board.

decisions.choice: Path rules plus runtime markers plus build check
decisions.rationale: Ban work-items <-> labels imports and any import of modules/board/** internals; server-only on rsc.ts and server/**; acyclic module-graph check; a production build must fail when a Client Component imports a server surface. Path legality and bundle safety are separate guarantees.

risks: Whole-board rejection on a single forbidden label is strict UX; if product prefers per-item degradation, the change is confined to application/load-board.ts, but that reading contradicts the task's 'reject' wording so it should be confirmed.

The task does not specify behavior for `missing` label ids. Assumption: excluded from the projection and carried as unresolvedLabelIds on the view rather than failing the read; switch to a `contract` failure if referential integrity is guaranteed by the labels store.
Label resolution must remain a single batched call keyed by distinct ids; a per-item adapter call would reintroduce N+1 behind an otherwise clean seam.

Loading all board candidates including archived ones and filtering in the domain trades query efficiency for policy locality; revisit only by extending the work-items public filter with a board-supplied argument, not by moving the policy.
`board` can become a dumping ground for anything touching two capabilities — admit new behavior only via the same deletion test that justified it.
Requires labels/server.ts to expose forbidden ids explicitly. If it currently filters them silently, that contract change is a prerequisite and touches a capability outside board's change authority.

Board's `status` and label-detail contracts duplicate vocabulary owned by work-items and labels; if those contracts drift, the mapping lives in the private adapters — resist promoting shared types into shared/kernel without identical meaning, lifecycle, and a named owner.

decisions.choice: Create src/modules/board/ as an orchestrating capability; reject both composing stores in the page and work-items calling labels
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code moves archived filtering, status grouping, ID-dependent sequencing, and the forbidden-label authorization consequence into app/**, which fails the deletion test and the app/** import rule. Work-items calling labels would embed label visibility policy and its rejection consequence in work-items, coupling two capabilities the task requires to stay independently changeable.

decisions.choice: Board owns no tables, no store, no server persistence module — only private adapters over work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts
decisions.rationale: Board has no data of its own; it is a projection. Declaring no table ownership makes any board-side .from()/.rpc() statically rejectable.

decisions.choice: labels/server.ts exposes resolveLabels(identity, ids) returning a complete { visible, missing, forbidden } resolution rather than a pre-filtered visible list
decisions.rationale: Authorization-sensitive joins require a complete non-enumerating resolution. A pre-filtered list would make the forbidden case indistinguishable from absent, so board could not reject; forbidden/missing echo only caller-supplied IDs to avoid enumeration.

decisions.choice: Any forbidden reference fails the whole board load closed as a typed { outcome: 'forbidden' } value
decisions.rationale: Policy requires rejection, and silent omission is explicitly disallowed. Stated as an assumption; the alternative is an explicit per-card restricted-label domain marker, never a silent drop.

decisions.choice: Keep application/load-board.ts with BoardWorkItems and BoardLabels role ports in board vocabulary
decisions.rationale: It owns real policy, cross-capability orchestration, a combining projection, and ID-dependent sequencing — not a forwarding call. Ports use board types; adapters map the source capabilities' public contracts.

decisions.choice: Only board/rsc.ts plus the route; no actions.ts, client/, ui/, query-cache.ts, stream.ts, or job.ts
decisions.rationale: The task has one server-rendered read and no mutation or browser query path; empty or speculative segments and surfaces are not created.

decisions.choice: page.tsx is the single capture owner: typed outcomes render, unexpected exceptions are reported once then rethrown to error.tsx
decisions.rationale: Trusted server.ts surfaces, loadBoard, and adapters stay silent so one unexpected failure is not reported twice; redirect/notFound stay outside generic catches.

decisions.choice: Authenticate in page.tsx; board read permission and label rejection in board application policy; label visibility in labels domain; tenant/ownership predicates in each source store under RLS
decisions.rationale: Three-layer defense in depth; trusted server.ts surfaces accept explicit identity and never rediscover the current user.

flows: RSC read: app/(app)/boards/[boardId]/page.tsx validates { boardId } locally -> shared/server/request-identity.ts derives verified actor/roles/tenant/requestId/traceId from the cookie session -> board/rsc.ts getBoardView(identity, { boardId })
Orchestration: board/rsc.ts -> board/server/load-board-service.ts createBoardDeps(identity) -> board/application/load-board.ts loadBoard({ boardId }, deps)
Step 1-2: deps.workItems.listForBoard(boardId) -> board/domain/group-by-status.ts dropArchived + board/domain/label-refs.ts collectLabelRefs -> label ID set

Step 3-5 (sequenced on derived IDs): deps.labels.resolve(ids) -> { visible, missing, forbidden }; forbidden.length > 0 returns { outcome: 'forbidden' }; otherwise groupByStatus(items, visible) returns { outcome: 'ok', view }

Adapter edge: board/server/work-items-adapter.ts -> work-items/server.ts listBoardWorkItems(identity, { boardId }) -> work-items/server/work-items-store.ts (RLS + tenant predicates), rows mapped to WorkItem then to board BoardItem
Adapter edge: board/server/labels-adapter.ts -> labels/server.ts resolveLabels(identity, ids) -> labels/domain/visibility.ts + labels/server/labels-store.ts, mapped to the board's own resolution type

Failure path: adapter maps provider error to unavailable/contract without reporting -> loadBoard and server.ts surfaces propagate silently -> page.tsx reports once and rethrows -> app/(app)/boards/[boardId]/error.tsx renders
Render path: page.tsx maps the typed outcome to app/(app)/boards/[boardId]/_components/ (columns, card, denied state) using only the public BoardView contract
risks: The forbidden-label policy is an assumption: whole-board rejection vs. an explicit per-card restricted marker changes the BoardView contract and the RSC render branch. Confirm with product before implementing.

If labels/server.ts is implemented as a filtered visible-only list (the easier shape), board silently drops forbidden references and the security requirement is unenforceable — this contract must be reviewed and tested directly at labels/server.ts.

Board sequences two reads (work-items then labels), so latency is additive by design; the labels call cannot be parallelized because it depends on IDs from the first result. Cap the label ID batch at the labels/server.ts contract to bound the second query.

Cache invalidation stays private in each source capability's server/**; board owns no tags, so a stale board view is diagnosed in work-items or labels, not in board. Do not let board grow its own tag wiring.
board/application/ports.ts must not drift into importing types from work-items/server.ts or labels/server.ts; without a lint rule the adapters' mapping layer tends to be short-circuited over time.

If a future board mutation (drag to change status) arrives, it belongs in a board actions.ts delegating to a work-items mutation surface — not in the RSC path, and not by giving work-items knowledge of labels.
Board reads no tables today; a shortcut Supabase query inside board/server/** would bypass the source capabilities' policy. Enforce the declared table-ownership canary alongside RLS.
server-only markers plus a production build are the only runtime guard against a Client Component importing board/rsc.ts; a missing build gate silently permits server-surface leakage.
response.summary: Create src/modules/board/ as an orchestrating capability rather than composing work-items and labels stores in the page or letting work-items call labels — the stakeholder preference conflicts with ownership, security, and change isolation. Board owns no persistence: board/application/load-board.ts holds the policy (drop archived, group by status, attach visible labels, reject forbidden label references) behind board-language ports, and private adapters in board/server/** call work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts. labels/server.ts must return a complete non-enumerating { visible, missing, forbidden } resolution so board can reject rather than silently omit. The single channel is app/(app)/boards/[boardId]/page.tsx via a server-only board/rsc.ts: it authenticates, maps typed outcomes to renderable state, and is the one owner of unexpected-failure reporting while inner surfaces stay silent. work-items and labels never import board or each other, keeping the module graph acyclic.

Framework boundary that renders after the channel rethrows an unexpected defect

Pure BoardView/BoardColumn/BoardCard/BoardLabel types and status column ordering
Pure archived filtering, grouping by status, and attachment of visible label details

BoardWorkItems and BoardLabels role ports expressed in board vocabulary and board types; imports no other capability's root surface types
The orchestrating operation: sequences the work-items read, derives label IDs, resolves labels, rejects forbidden references, returns a typed board outcome; framework-neutral and silent
Private adapter implementing BoardWorkItems over work-items/server.ts, mapping WorkItem into board types and provider errors into semantic failures
Private adapter implementing BoardLabels over labels/server.ts, mapping the label resolution into the board's own type and mapping identity separately for this source
Capability-local typed factory that wires identity and concrete adapters into the dependency object loadBoard needs

Work-item invariants including status and archived semantics
Private Supabase store owning the work_items table with tenant/ownership predicates under RLS and row-to-domain mapping
Trusted silent surface listBoardWorkItems(identity, { boardId }) returning domain work items with labelIds; consumed only by board's work-items adapter
Label domain value distinct from provider rows
Label visibility policy owned by labels, evaluated against the explicit actor
Private store owning the labels table with tenant/ownership predicates under RLS

Derives the verified actor, roles, tenant scope, requestId, and traceId together with the cookie-scoped client from one session
